The entry records an opinion survey, not a legal finding. Its central figures should therefore be understood as respondents' reported beliefs and judgments, rather than proof of financial misconduct. corrected_draft.title: Trump Sued Over Selling Early Access to Truth Social Posts
corrected_draft.description_short: Trump Sued Over Selling Early Access to Truth Social Posts
corrected_draft.description_medium: A federal lawsuit has been filed against President Donald Trump, accusing him of violating the First Amendment by selling special advance access to his Truth Social posts. The lawsuit claims that this practice is unconstitutional and gives certain individuals unfair access to the president's thoughts and ideas.
corrected_draft.description_long: A federal lawsuit filed in the Southern District of New York on August 12, 2026, accused the Trump administration of violating the First Amendment by selling advance access to Truth Social posts. The plaintiffs were the Freedom of the Press Foundation and The Intercept, represented by several legal organizations. Their complaint challenged Truth API, a service announced by Truth Social’s parent company that offered early access to posts by Trump and other officials for as much as $100,000 per month; the report said at least 10 customers had signed up. The plaintiffs argued that the president was monetizing public statements and providing market-moving government information to paying users. The report noted that Trump held a 41% stake in Trump Media & Technology Group through a trust controlled by one of his sons, and that the administration had treated his Truth Social posts as official presidential statements in other contexts. These are allegations in a newly filed case, not a court ruling. The White House had not responded to the request for comment when the report was published.

corrected_draft.title: OCC gives World Liberty Trust conditional preliminary approval for a bank charter
corrected_draft.description_short: OCC gives World Liberty Trust conditional preliminary approval for a bank charter
corrected_draft.description_medium: The supplied reporting describes preliminary conditional OCC approval for World Liberty Trust Company to pursue a national trust bank charter. Further conditions remained; the company was not yet authorized to operate as a bank.
corrected_draft.description_long: World Liberty Trust Company, an entity associated with World Liberty Financial, received preliminary conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in August 2026 to pursue a national trust bank charter. The OCC letter says the application met certain regulatory and policy requirements, but it makes clear that additional conditions must be satisfied before the company can open and conduct the proposed fiduciary business. This is not the same as an unconditional charter or a finding that the firm is already operating as a national bank. The crypto venture was launched by Trump and his sons, making the proposed institution a source of conflict-of-interest concerns because the president and his family have financial interests in the company. Those concerns are political and ethical questions; the approval letter itself does not find misconduct. HuffPost described the development as preliminary approval, and Bloomberg reported that the applicant was World Liberty Trust Co. The accurate event is a regulator’s conditional step in a chartering process. Future operations depend on the company meeting requirements and receiving the remaining permissions, so the title’s shorthand should not imply a completed bank launch.
